recentItems.title: Hundreds of thousands expected in Paris for Pope Leo XIV visit to France | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Pope Leo XIV embarks on a four-day visit to France on Friday, with the highpoint being a giant Mass attended by more than half a million people in central Paris.
 
For Saturday's afternoon celebration, an altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde and a large area around the Champs-Élysées sealed off by police.
 
President Emmanuel Macron greeted the Pope at Orly airport on Friday morning, and is due to hold talks with him at the Élysée Palace on geopolitical issues and artificial intelligence (AI) later. He will also deliver a speech with the Pope in Metz.
 
However, the president will not be at any of the Pope's Masses, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.

What Trump and Xi dined on at the White House state dinner | BBC News
recentItems.description:
The office of the First Lady Melania Trump released details of the menu for Thursday's White House state dinner, which it describes as a showcase of "American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence".
 
Dining at the White House alongside the two world leaders were some of the most notable names in tech, including Apple’s Tim Cook, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Jensen Huang of Nvidia.

recentItems.title: The world’s two most powerful men just met. How did it go? #BBCNews
Trump hosts China's Xi at White House state dinner | BBC News
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania have welcomed China's Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan to the White House for a state dinner.
 
Earlier, Trump said he and Xi had made "tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries"; Xi, meanwhile, said he hoped "Chinese companies are treated fairly here".
 
Some of the most notable names in tech, including Satya Nadella of Microsoft, Apple’s Tim Cook, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Jensen Huang of Nvidia, are dining alongside the world leaders at the White House.

recentItems.title: Delegates walk out before Netanyahu’s address to UN General Assembly | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told the UN General Assembly “we have crushed Iran’s military”, after dozens of delegates left the chamber and refused to listen to his address.
 
In Washington, US President Donald Trump is hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has asked him to return to the ceasefire agreed with Iran in June.
 
Meanwhile, Saudi-led forces have said the Iran-backed Houthis fired six missiles at two Saudi Arabian cities. And Iran has threatened to paralyse airports in neighbouring countries if they stop commercial Iranian flights in response to US aviation sanctions.
